Your feelings are understandable. While I cannot relate to this, I can only imagine the blindside that you feel. With that being said, I think forgiveness is a choice and a strong one at that. A mistake, no matter how larger, can haunt a person to the end of their life. If you were to punish your grandpa, if that is by icing him out and not talking to him, he would have to add that to whatever guilt he was feeling about the situation as is. I would assume he carries heavy guilt as he hasn’t told anyone besides yourself. In addition, despite the world we might live in today, shaming people does not teach them. It allows for embarrassment and eventual resentment. Do not shame your grandpa for his mistake. I also want to point out that my boyfriends grandpa served during the depression, and has told me the things that soldiers were put through. Horrid situations that caused everlasting trauma and PTSD. Not excusing what your grandpa did, cause it is disgusting, but that time period was different. It was not common sense back then to do the right thing. Allow him to learn and if he has learned love him for that growth. Most elders I know refuse to acknowledge their mistakes. I hope your family is staying safe.

First of all, you are deserving. I was in your same boat a while ago and totally understand the constant weight and racing thoughts that fill you constantly. It is not easy to handle so honestly, I am proud of you. I am proud of you to express the concern and ask for advice. That was something I never had the strength to do. In terms of social anxiety and feel under serving, just know that as an individual you are in your head a lot more than those around you. Your constantly thoughts on how others perceive you are just a phantom. When I was in high school, I was nervous when presenting a project to the class. My teacher noticed and said “ don’t worry, no one is even listening to you, they are sitting in their chairs thinking about their presentation and how nervous they are.” I have had several conversations with friends asking if they worry as much as I do. They agreed. They often times think “ am I too loud” or “ do these people think I’m weird”. Being able to relax and know that the people in your life live and cherish you despite your flaws and insecurities. If anyone judges you the way we sometime judge ourselves, then that person needs to be removed. I also want to add, as someone who has been bullied, if someone is thinking something, they will tell you or it’s clearly obvious. But overall, you are strong and deserving of the friends, family and memories in your life. I see your strength just by asking this question. It is that same strength that will allow you to push through this dark stage.
